question: In 2017, as part of phase 1 of the SIBMMIL programme, the European Commission called on Italy to establish an EU-funded Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Libya. The money has been spent, but when I asked about it in 2021, neither the Council nor the Commission were able to say where this equipment is located.

The Italian Ministry of the Interior has not been able to provide an explanation to journalists either. That same year, the EU launched phase 2 of the programme, and delivered an additional mobile, container-based MRCC. Various militias are now quarrelling over the equipment, meaning that it has yet to become operational. 1.
Where exactly is the equipment that was delivered under phase 1 of the SIBMMIL programme for a MRCC in Tripoli, and to what extent is this MRCC operating as planned?
If, in the HR/VP’s view, the MRCC in Tripoli is not yet operational, what shortcomings need to be resolved, and what efforts is the HR/VP making to this end?

Who is in charge of the container delivered in phase 2 of the SIBMMIL programme, and which Libyan units (coastal guard, navy, maritime police or other militias) are to operate them, in which location?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.3.2024) The establishment of a new and improved Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) is fundamental to facilitate the tasks of relevant authorities in the area of search and rescue, and hence save lives at sea.

In particular, the MRCC will help better organising search and rescue operations by the Libyan coast guard and the General Administration for Coastal Security, ensuring coordination with other actors (e.g., commercial coastal traffic, neighbouring countries), and overall making the response quicker in case of emergencies in the Libyan search and rescue zone.

In terms of the equipment provided, it includes a container unit, a mobile unit, training and coaching of the official MRCC staff. These have been delivered and are currently stored in the port of Tripoli under the control of the Libyan port authority, as also verified by a recent EU mission.

Moreover, the site for the mobile MRCC has been identified by Libyan authorities inside the commercial port of Tripoli, works to connect the utilities (e.g., water and electricity) have started and should be completed soon.
